notes: PDF-only review. This paper studies 39 high-latitude B-type stars and 447 Galactic open clusters to identify possible birth clusters and runaway ejection mechanisms. The paper's candidate language refers to star-cluster trajectory matches or candidate parent clusters, not stars treated as possibly unbound from the Milky Way. Table 2 reports ejection probabilities and characteristics for 16 orphan-parent matches; v_eject is the velocity relative to the potential birth cluster at the time of intersection, with values about 37-160 km/s, not a Galactic rest-frame speed or escape/boundness quantity. The word unbound appears in the binary-supernova discussion only for a secondary becoming unbound from the compact remnant, not unbound from the Galaxy. EC 05438-4741 is discussed as a high-latitude star whose trajectory did not approach the disk within 50 Myr and as a possible halo-origin object, but after extending to 100 Myr the paper says it appears to originate from the disk after all and does not claim a Galactic escape or unbound HVS status. Therefore no objects meet the benchmark definition of HVS/unbound-from-Galaxy candidates.
